ownership_decision.invariant: Publishing owns publisher names, publications and their releases; a release is immutable and pins one version and its content hash.

boundary_decision.interaction: Publishing resolves the caller's workspace through Identity, and reads Registry's Skill and Version facts and takes Registry's Skill lock only through functions the composition root injects.

domain_forces: Disclosing a Skill publicly is a different promise from the catalog vouching for it, so publishing cannot be a flag on the Skill.
A publication must keep showing what was released even as the author adds versions, and must stop showing it the moment governance says so.
implementation_design.decision: A new context owns publisher, publication and release records; the release is an append-only row pinning version and hash, and the public read re-checks the pinned Skill's governance facts every time instead of copying them.
invariants_preserved: Registry owns Skill and Version facts, takedowns and holds.
rejected_alternatives: A published flag on the Skill: it cannot hold a namespace, a permanent name or the history of what was released.
Copy the governance verdict into the release: a takedown would not reach an address that is already public.

record.name: Publishing
record.responsibility: Owns who discloses what under which name: a creator's publisher namespace, the publications in it, and the immutable releases that pin the version each one shows.

record.rationale: Every user-data query resolves its Workspace scope here; this is the single entry point that makes workspace scoping enforceable.

approvals.scope: Publishing as a new core context owning publisher names, publications and immutable releases, allowed to query Identity for workspace scope
